append.text: **Ps 74:3 *cum accépero tempus* → *quando tomar o tempo*** — a local departure to *tomar* (17:17's verb): God takes the time, he does not receive it (λάβω καιρόν; DRB 'when I shall take a time'); *quando receber o tempo* would make it given to him. The ambiguity reader heard 'when I find the time' first; *no tempo que eu tiver fixado* (MS1932) is the option. No Latinist remark on either run.

**Ps 74:5, 74:6, 74:11 → *o chifre … o vosso chifre … os chifres dos pecadores … os chifres do justo*** — kept five times; the Latinist passed it twice; the stylist named the cuckold connotation and said the image must stay; the ambiguity reader heard literal horn / cuckold first and listed 'chifre as power' unknown. The image stands unexplained, as in the Latin.

**Ps 74:3 *ego justítias judicábo* (εὐθύτητας) → *eu julgarei as justiças*** — the internal object kept with the row's plural; the ambiguity reader heard 'judge with justice' (right) but found the plural puzzling and listed it unknown; the Latinist passed it twice. *com justiça* (MS1932) and *retamente* (57:2) options.

**Ps 74:4 *ego confirmávi colúmnas ejus* → *eu firmei as suas colunas*** — a thing set fast, the row's *firmar* (ἐστερέωσα); passed every reader. More evidence for *firmar* except where a word is confirmed.

**Ps 74:5 *Dixi iníquis: Nolíte iníque ágere* → *Eu disse aos iníquos: Não ajais iniquamente*** — the adverb (not the neuter plural) and the Latin's echo *iníquis … iníque* (Greek παρανομοῦσιν μὴ παρανομεῖτε) kept; the ambiguity reader listed *ajais* and *iniquamente* unknown; Latinist and stylist silent. *Não procedais iniquamente* option.

**Ps 74:5 *Nolíte exaltáre cornu* → *Não exalteis o chifre*; 74:11 *exaltabúntur córnua justi* → *serão exaltados os chifres do justo*** — one verb as the frame of the psalm (74:8 *exáltat → exalta* between); *levantar* (DRB) refused (leváre's). No reader remarked.
**Ps 74:6 *Nolíte extóllere in altum cornu vestrum* → *Não ergais para o alto o vosso chifre*** — applied; the ambiguity reader listed *ergais* unknown (the form, not the verb).

**Ps 74:8 *calix in manu Dómini vini meri plenus misto* → *na mão do Senhor há um cálice de vinho puro, cheio de mistura*** — *há* supplied; the paradox kept (merum → *puro*, mistum → *mistura*). The ambiguity reader heard the Eucharistic chalice first and the paradox as a contradiction, as the Latin is.

**Ps 74:9 *fæx ejus non est exinaníta* → *a sua borra não foi esgotada*** — D41's word for dregs of the cup; *exinaníre* → *esgotar* (passive taken from the Latinist; his *esvaziada* option). The ambiguity reader listed *borra* unknown.
Ps 74:10 *Ego autem annuntiábo* → *Eu, porém, anunciarei*, as 58:17 *Ego autem cantábo* (the same turn); the stylist named it the best line.
Ps 74:9 → *todavia*, inside a colon; no reader remarked.

**Ps 74:6 *nolíte loqui advérsus Deum iniquitátem* → *não faleis iniquidade contra Deus*** — the content object kept; the stylist heard *falar iniquidade* as a calque and asked *digais* (option; *dizer* is dícere's, 74:5 *Dixi*). The Latinist passed it twice.
Ps 74:7 *quóniam Deus judex est* → *pois Deus é juiz* (49:6's build, no article).
Ps 74:11 *ómnia córnua peccatórum confríngam* → *quebrarei todos os chifres dos pecadores* (συγκλάσω); alone in the psalm; no reader remarked.

terms: | liquefácere (*liquefácta est terra*) | derreter-se (*Derreteu-se a terra*) | open | Ps 74:4 (ἐτάκη; 21:15b *cera que se derrete* is liquéscere). Concrete, as the Greek's melting; MS1932 *dissolveu-se* option. The ambiguity reader heard it literally, 'a strange image' — the Latin's. |

| merum / mistum (*vini meri plenus misto*) | vinho puro / mistura (*um cálice de vinho puro, cheio de mistura*) | open | Ps 74:8 (οἴνου ἀκράτου πλῆρες κεράσματος; DRB 'strong wine full of mixture'). The paradox kept unexplained. |

| exinaníre | esgotar (of dregs: *a sua borra não foi esgotada*) | open | Ps 74:9 (ἐξεκενώθη). MS1932's verb; *esvaziar* (the root sense, the Latinist's) option. 136:7 *Exinaníte, exinaníte* (razing a city) decides for itself — *esvaziar* / *arrasar* there. |

| hic … hic (distributive: *Hunc humíliat, et hunc exáltat*; *ex hoc in hoc*) | este … aquele (*A este humilha, e àquele exalta*; *deste para aquele*) | open | Ps 74:8–9 (τοῦτον … τοῦτον). *a este … a este* is not the Portuguese idiom and can be heard as one man; MS1932 has *este … aquele*. The literal repetition and DRB's *um … outro* are options. No reader remarked. |

| desértus (adj., *desértis móntibus*) | deserto (*dos montes desertos*) | open | Ps 74:7 (ἐρήμων ὀρέων; DRB 'desert hills'; the Hebrew's 'desert of the mountains' not followed). The noun desértum stays *deserto* (28:7). |
